meta.title: Planting Trees in the Nature Park
meta.textType: a school text with five paragraph topics

paragraphs: Planting Trees in the Nature Park, posted by May. On Saturday, the Explorers helped Ranger Mark in the nature park. One area of the forest was empty, because the old trees were gone. The park needed new trees in that place. It was a hot morning, but the forest was cool. We wore hats, boots, and long trousers. Teacher Kim and four adults came with us. There were nearly twenty children, and the work was big.

At eight o'clock, a truck came to the park gate. It delivered one hundred small trees. Each tree was in a black bag with earth. The bags were heavy, so we carried them in pairs. The trees were only as tall as my knee. A park worker put them in a long line under a big tree. Leo counted them twice, and the number was right.

Ranger Mark told us about the trees. He had a list of local trees on a big paper. "These trees are local," he said. "They grow here in nature, and the birds and insects know them." A foreign tree comes from a place that is far away. The park is against foreign trees, because they can hurt the local plants. The usual way in this park is simple: plant only local trees. Mia asked, "Do you ever plant a foreign tree?" "No, never," said Ranger Mark with a smile.

Each adult worked with three children. Ranger Mark showed us how to plant a tree. First, make a hole in the ground. Then take the small tree out of the bag. Put it in the hole, and push the earth around it. Leo made a deep hole, and he was very proud. I put water on the earth when my tree was in. I was nervous, because I did not want to hurt my tree. Mia was nervous too, but one of the adults smiled and helped her.

At noon, we sat under a big tree and ate lunch. We planted thirty trees in the morning. Ranger Mark put a small wooden sign next to the first tree. The sign said, "Planted by the Explorers." Lily took a photo of every tree for the blog. Teacher Kim said, "You worked well today." Then we walked back to the gate with dirty hands and happy faces. In a few years, these trees will be taller than all of us. I want to visit this area every year.
text.summary: May writes about the day when the Explorers plant trees in the nature park. A truck brings a hundred small trees, Ranger Mark explains why the trees must be local, and the Explorers plant thirty of them before lunch.
